nora: Heads up everyone 1 - launching two billing updates next quarter: "Usage Smoothing Credits" and a machine-readable invoice JSON export. Goal is clearer invoices + fewer surprise bills.

nora: Usage Smoothing Credits (USC): for customers with consistent weekly usage patterns we'll apply a small automated credit each invoice to offset burst noise. It's targeted, not universal. Effective for invoices with period starting 2026-11-01.

jasper: What's "consistent weekly usage" mean programmatically?

nora: Metric: coefficient of variation of daily hosted token usage <= 0.25 over a trailing 30-day window AND monthly volume > 100k tokens. If eligible, USC = min(3% of token charges, $30). Applies after promo credits.

toni: Important: does this change quotas or limits?

nora: No. USC affects billing only. Quotas, rate limits, and Dedicated commitments unchanged. Abuse detection still enforced as usual.

billing-bot: Sample invoice fragment:
```
2026-11-01 to 2026-11-30 - Hosted usage: 540,000 tokens
Promotional credits applied: -$25.00
Usage Smoothing Credit (USC): -$11.30 (eligible under weekly stability rule)
Amount due: $X.XX
```

cs-lead: We'll need a support macro and a short FAQ. Suggested macro: "If your account is eligible for an automatic Usage Smoothing Credit, you'll see it as a line on your invoice called 'Usage Smoothing Credit'. This does not affect your rate limits. For questions email billing@redwood.ai."

jasper: How will we explain edge cases to enterprise customers with hybrid Dedicated + Hosted usage?

nora: USC only evaluates hosted billed tokens. For mixed accounts we'll show a hosted-only subtotal and the USC line beneath it. Enterprise contracts with explicit invoice terms are exempt unless sales/legal sign off.

nora: Second update: machine-readable invoice JSON export. Customers can download a canonical JSON representation of their invoice (line items, SKU, model_sku, credits, adjustments) to simplify cost allocation and automated chargebacks.

toni: Any PII risks in the JSON export?

legal: Reviewed 1 - the export will not include raw request traces, only aggregated billing fields (line_id, sku, model_sku, tokens, unit_price, line_total). We added a clause to the billing policy that exports may be redacted for sensitive accounts on request.

billing-bot: Example JSON fields returned (humanized):
```
{"invoice_id":"inv_202611_0001","lines":[{"line_id":"L1","description":"Hosted API - rwd-v1-small","model_sku":"rwd-v1-small","tokens":300000,"unit_price":0.00004,"line_total":12.00}],"credits":[{"type":"promo","amount":25.00}],"usage_smoothing_credit":11.30}
```

cs-lead: Support: add KB for consuming the JSON export (sample code snippets, curl example, Python). We'll also add a one-click CSV from JSON option in the UI.

jasper: Any impact on billing exports or existing SFTP feeds?

nora: Existing CSV/SFTP feeds are unchanged. The JSON export is additive. Finance-eng will add a schema version header so automation can detect changes.

toni: Timeline?

nora: Feature rollout: internal beta next week, limited customer beta in two weeks, general availability 2026-11-01. Finance will publish the JSON schema in the billing docs.

legal: Note: update TOS addendum for the new export and automatic USC eligibility rules. Also, don't promise USC amounts until they appear on an invoice.

cs-lead: We'll prepare templated customer comms and an opt-out flow for customers that prefer not to have automated credits applied.

nora: Thanks all. If you see exceptions (resellers, aggregated orgs, prepaid accounts) add them to the tracker in the doc and tag me.
